subtitle: The inland battle that broke a sea-born dream

panels.shot: split-panel wide, half showing a dusty South Indian plain with armies facing off, half a stormy sea with warships locked in distant battle
panels.action: Eyre Coote stands firm in red-coated uniform on a parched field near Vandavasi as Comte de Lally, in white French dress with blue facings, glares from the opposite side, while ghostly silhouettes of ships loom over the horizon behind them.

dialogue.text: In January 1760, on the dry earth of Wandiwash, Eyre Coote and Comte de Lally fought a battle that did not end French India alone, but slammed shut one of its last open roads.

i18n.hi: जनवरी 1760 में सूखे वांडीवाश पर, आयर कूट और कॉन्त दे लाली ने ऐसी लड़ाई लड़ी, जिसने सिर्फ फ़्रेंच इंडिया नहीं, उसकी आख़िरी बची राह भी बंद कर दी।

panels.shot: high wide shot over a map-table, slowly pushing in
panels.action: A parchment map of the Carnatic and Coromandel coast lies on a wooden table, marked with Pondicherry, Madras, Wandiwash and lines of march, as candlelight and the shadows of unseen hands fall across it.

dialogue.text: Before the dust of Wandiwash rose, ink and orders had already drawn the lines: Pondicherry against Madras, French Company against English Company, both feeding off Indian wars and rivalries.

i18n.hi: वांडीवाश की धूल उठने से पहले ही, स्याही और हुक्म से लकीरें खिंच चुकी थीं: पोंडीचेरी बनाम मद्रास, फ़्रेंच कम्पनी बनाम इंग्लिश कम्पनी, दोनों ही भारतीय जंगों और दुश्मनियों पर पलते हुए।

panels.shot: alternating close-ups, split diagonally between two faces
panels.action: On one side Eyre Coote, calm, sun-browned, in plain but well-kept red coat, leans over a dispatch; on the other, Comte de Lally, stern and tired-eyed, in a white French officer’s coat, reads a letter with tightened jaw.

dialogue.text: Eyre Coote, a rising Company soldier hardened in Bengal, wrote of positions, supplies and discipline. Lally, veteran of European wars, wrote of broken promises, empty magazines and a navy that never came in time.

i18n.hi: बंगाल में सख़्त हो चुका कम्पनी अफ़सर आयर कूट ठिकानों, रसद और अनुशासन की बात लिखता है। यूरोपीय जंगों का बूढ़ा शेर लाली टूटे वादों, खाली गोदामों और कभी समय पर न आई नौसेना की शिकायत करता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Coote in council tent, low angle to show resolve
panels.action: Inside a canvas tent on the Madras plain, Eyre Coote stands over a rough table before Indian allies and Company officers, pointing toward a marked spot labeled Wandiwash on the map, his expression controlled but intent.

dialogue.text: By late 1759, Coote knew the French still held a chain of inland posts. Among them, Wandiwash stood as a fortified link to Pondicherry. Cut that link, and the pressure on Madras would ease.

i18n.hi: 1759 के आख़िर तक कूट जानता था कि फ़्रांसीसियों की ज़मीन में अब भी एक कड़ी बची है। उनमें वांडीवाश पोंडीचेरी से जुड़ा किला था। बस ये कड़ी काट दो, तो मद्रास पर दबाव हल्का हो जाएगा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Lally addressing French officers and Indian allies in a hall at Pondicherry
panels.action: In a high-ceilinged hall in Pondicherry, Lally stands before French officers and Indian sepoys, with a few Indian chiefs in fine robes, gesturing sharply toward an inland direction as maps and reports lie scattered.

dialogue.text: At Pondicherry, Lally was pulled between sea and land. The French fleet had lost command of the coast, money and grain arrived late, yet Paris demanded offensive war. He turned inland, toward Wandiwash, to break the English hold.

i18n.hi: पोंडीचेरी में लाली समंदर और ज़मीन के बीच फँसा था। फ़्रेंच बेड़ा किनारे की हकूमत हार चुका था, रुपया–अनाज देर से आता, पर पेरिस को हमला ही हमला चाहिए था। वो अंदर की ओर, वांडीवाश की तरफ़ मुड़ा, अंग्रेज़ों की पकड़ तोड़ने।

panels.shot: wide shot of marching columns approaching Wandiwash fort at dawn
panels.action: At grey dawn, long files of British redcoats, sepoys and cavalry under Coote move across scrubland toward the distant stone fort of Wandiwash, while far off another column’s dust plume marks the French approach under Lally.

dialogue.text: So both commanders converged. Coote came to seize the fort and draw the French out. Lally marched with his best European troops and Indian allies to strike the English field army before it grew stronger.

i18n.hi: दोनों सरदार एक ही मैदान पर खिंच आए। कूट किला लेने और फ़्रांसीसियों को बाहर खींचने चला। लाली अपने चुने हुए यूरोपीय सिपाहियों और भारतीय साथी फौज के साथ निकला, ताकि अंग्रेज़ मैदान फ़ौज को बढ़ने से पहले ही तोड़ दे।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the battlefield layout, diagrammatic feel but still naturalistic
panels.action: From high above, the dry plain near Wandiwash stretches out, with the English line of red-coated infantry and sepoys forming before a village and tank, and the French line deploying opposite with cavalry on the flanks and guns between.

dialogue.text: Orme’s pages and Coote’s dispatch sketch the field: a hard, open plain, a tank and village near the English right, French cannon facing them, cavalry waiting on the wings, and the old fort watching in silence.

i18n.hi: ओर्म की किताब और कूट की चिट्ठियाँ मैदान का नक्शा बनाती हैं: सख़्त, खुला समतल, दाईं तरफ़ अंग्रेज़ों के पास तालाब और गाँव, सामने तने फ़्रेंच तोप, पंखों पर घुड़सवार, और पुराना किला चुपचाप देखता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot on Coote on horseback, scanning the French line
panels.action: Coote sits his horse calmly at the English front, spyglass in hand, studying the French alignment as sepoys adjust turbans and redcoats fix bayonets in the rising heat.

dialogue.text: Coote wrote of French bravery but also of their haste. He noted where their guns stood, where the ground sloped, and how his sepoys and cavalry could be used without wasting European infantry.

i18n.hi: कूट ने फ़्रांसीसियों की बहादुरी लिखी, पर उनकी जल्दबाज़ी भी। उसने नोट किया कहाँ उनकी तोपें जमीं, कहाँ ज़मीन ढलान थी, और कैसे उसके सिपाही व सवार बिना यूरोपीय पैदल को झोंके खेले जा सकते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot on Lally and Bussy in the French line, slight low angle
panels.action: Lally, mounted and rigid-backed, confers briefly with another French officer, Bussy, who gestures toward the English position, as French infantry in white and Indian allies form up behind them.

dialogue.text: Lally, with Bussy by his side, saw another picture. His army was smaller than he wished, the sea unsafe, yet he believed a bold stroke could still humble the Company in the Carnatic.

i18n.hi: लाली, बुस्सी को साथ लेकर, दूसरा मंजर देखता है। फौज मनचाही से कम, समंदर असुरक्षित, पर उसे यक़ीन था कि एक जोरदार वार अब भी कम्पनी को कर्नाटक में झुका सकता है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of cavalry engagement on a dusty flank
panels.action: On one flank, British allied cavalry and French-allied horsemen clash in a swirling cloud of dust, lances leveled and horses rearing, as infantry lines in the background hold steady under smoke from opening cannon fire.

dialogue.text: The first clashes were of horse and dust. Indian cavalry on both sides fought for the flanks, while French and English cannon began to trade fire, each commander testing the other’s nerve and ground.

i18n.hi: पहले टकराव घोड़ों और धूल के थे। दोनों तरफ़ की भारतीय घुड़सवारियाँ पंखों पर भिड़ीं, जबकि फ़्रेंच और इंग्लिश तोपें बोलने लगीं, दोनों सरदार एक–दूजे की हिम्मत और ज़मीन आज़माते हुए।

panels.shot: tight shot on a French powder cart and caisson amid the artillery line
panels.action: Near the French guns, a powder caisson stands close behind a cannon, barrels and bags piled high, gunners rushing to and fro as a stray spark or shot approaches unseen.

dialogue.text: Then came the blast the records agree on. A French powder caisson, loaded and too close to the guns, took a shot or spark. In a moment the air over their line was thick with fire and flying earth.

i18n.hi: फिर वो धमाका आया जिस पर सारी रिपोर्टें एक हैं। एक फ़्रेंच बारूद गाड़ी, भरी हुई और तोपों के बहुत पास, किसी गोली या चिंगारी से फट पड़ी। पल में उनकी कतार के ऊपर की हवा आग और उड़ी हुई मिट्टी से भर गई।

panels.shot: wide shot from behind the English line, showing the distant explosion in the French rear
panels.action: From behind the English infantry, we see a towering cloud of smoke and debris rising in the French position as men scatter and artillery pieces are thrown askew, while Coote and his officers watch keenly.

dialogue.text: Coote’s dispatch coolly notes the explosion and its effect on French order. A gap opened in their center. For a brief time, command, communication and confidence burned as hot as the powder itself.

i18n.hi: कूट की ठंडी चिट्ठी उस धमाके और उससे फ़्रांसीसी सफ़ की टूटी क़ायदे को दर्ज करती है। उनके बीच में बड़ा दराड़ खुल गई। थोड़ी देर को हुक्म, खबर और हिम्मत सब उसी बारूद की तरह तपने लगे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Coote giving an order, troops surging forward behind
panels.action: Seizing the moment, Coote raises his sword and gives a crisp order as English infantry and sepoys begin an ordered advance, faces set, bayonets gleaming, toward the unsettled French line.

dialogue.speaker: Eyre Coote & Comte de Lally
dialogue.text: Forward now—steady, and strike where they waver.

i18n.hi: अब आगे बढ़ो—थमे रहो, और वहीं वार करो जहाँ वो डगमगाएँ।

panels.shot: wide shot of close musket volleys between the main infantry lines
panels.action: Two rigid infantry lines, French in white and British in red mixed with Indian sepoys, trade volleys at close range, smoke hanging heavy between them as men reload and officers shout over the din.

dialogue.text: The battle did not end with the blast. French troops and their Indian allies rallied and fought hard, but Coote’s line, well supplied and well drilled, pressed forward, using the opening to roll their enemy back.

i18n.hi: जंग सिर्फ उस धमाके पर नहीं रूकी। फ़्रेंच फौज और उनके भारतीय साथी फिर संभले और ज़ोर से लड़े, पर कूट की पंक्ति, भरपूर रसद और पक्की मश्क से, आगे धकेलती चली गई, उसी दरार से दुश्मन को उलटते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bussy surrounded and disarmed, with Coote’s officers nearby
panels.action: Amid the confusion near the French center, Bussy is shown surrounded by British officers and sepoys, his sword lowered as he is taken into custody, his face a mix of anger and resignation.

dialogue.text: In that hard pushing back and forth, Bussy was taken prisoner. British accounts mark his capture as a prize; French writings remember it as another cruel stroke in a campaign already starved and isolated.

i18n.hi: उस सख़्त धक्का–मुक्की में बुस्सी क़ैदी बना। अंग्रेज़ी हिसाब उसे बड़ी गिरफ़्तारी लिखते हैं; फ़्रांसीसी लिखावटें उसे पहले से भूखी–कटी मुहिम पर एक और बेरहम चोट मानती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Lally overseeing a controlled withdrawal, face strained
panels.action: Lally, still mounted but with powder-stained coat, gestures urgently to his officers as French troops begin an orderly but reluctant withdrawal from the field, cannon being limbered and moved away under pressure.

dialogue.text: At last, with his line shaken, ammunition low and no hope of naval rescue on that inland field, Lally ordered retreat. Coote, in his dispatch, wrote of a clear victory. Lally later wrote of a forced withdrawal from an impossible position.

i18n.hi: आख़िर में, जब सफ़ हिल चुकी, गोलियाँ कम बचीं और उस सूखी ज़मीन पर समंदर से मदद की आस न रही, लाली ने पीछे हटने का हुक्म दिया। कूट ने अपनी रिपोर्ट में साफ़ जीत लिखी; लाली ने बाद में इसे नामुमकिन मोर्चे से मजबूरी की वापसी कहा।

panels.shot: long shot of the French column trudging back toward distant Pondicherry
panels.action: Under a harsh sun, the diminished French army marches away over the scrub, standards drooping slightly, as the faint outline of Pondicherry’s walls and church spires appears far on the horizon.

dialogue.text: From Wandiwash, Lally fell back toward Pondicherry. Coote and Orme saw this as the French field army broken. Lally’s own writings pinned blame on empty magazines, unpaid troops and a navy that had ceded the coast.

i18n.hi: वांडीवाश से लाली पोंडीचेरी की ओर पीछे लौटा। कूट और ओर्म के लिए ये फ़्रेंच मैदान फ़ौज का टूटना था। लाली की लिखत इस हार का दोष खाली गोदामों, नाकारा वेतन और किनारा छोड़ चुकी नौसेना पर डालती है।

panels.shot: split wide panel: left shows siege works before Pondicherry, right shows European diplomats at a treaty table
panels.action: On one side, Coote and allied forces dig trenches and raise batteries before the walls of Pondicherry; on the other, powdered European diplomats sit at a polished table in Europe, quills poised over a treaty draft.

dialogue.text: Wandiwash alone did not end French power in India. It crippled their land arm, cleared the way for Pondicherry’s fall in 1761, and weighed heavily when, in 1763, the Treaty of Paris left France with only trading posts.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ वांडीवाश ने फ़्रेंच की सारी ताक़त नहीं खत्म की। लेकिन उसने उनकी ज़मीनी बाँह तोड़ दी, 1761 में पोंडीचेरी की गिरावट का रास्ता साफ़ किया, और 1763 की पेरिस संधि पर भारी पड़ा, जब फ़्रांस के हिस्से बस कुछ कारखाने बचे।

panels.shot: close-up on an Indian chronicler’s hand writing by lamplight, faint reflections of Coote and Lally in the ink-well
panels.action: By lamplight, an Indian chronicler’s hand writes on palm leaf or paper, while in the dark ink we see faint reflections of Coote in red and Lally in white, their faces distant, as ships and forts blur together behind them.

dialogue.text: On that brown field near Vandavasi, an empire born on ships lost its inland breath. Coote saw tactical proof, Lally an unjust fate, but the plain itself shows how far-off seas and treaties can die in local dust.

i18n.hi: वंदवासी के उस भूरे मैदान पर, जहाज़ों पर जन्मी सल्तनत ने ज़मीन पर साँस हार दी। कूट को यहाँ चाल की सच्चाई दिखी, लाली को नाइंसाफ़ क़िस्मत, पर ये मैदान खुद बताता है कि दूर के समंदर और समझौते भी स्थानीय धूल में दम तोड़ देते हैं।
